title: Resident Evil breaks records with $60 million debut
seoTitle: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil reboot redefines game.
subtitle: Zach Cregger's reboot surpasses expectations and redefines game adaptations
excerpt: Zach Cregger's new Resident Evil opens the door to box office success, grossing $60 million on its opening weekend and breaking records.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The new Resident Evil, directed by Zach Cregger, opened the door to box office success, grossing US$60 million over the weekend, surpassing the previous record of US$26 million. The combination of positive reviews, word-of-mouth, and a focus on a more faithful gaming experience propelled the film to become the franchise's biggest launch in 24 years.

Why the Film is Trending Now

The unexpected success of Resident Evil is linked to the return of a well-received reboot after the failure of the last one in 2021. Director Zach Cregger, who previously impressed with Weapons, brought an approach that prioritizes the feeling of playing, rather than just reproducing game characters. This shift in focus generated favorable reviews and strong audience recommendation, resulting in a debut that exceeded expectations.

Box Office Record and Franchise Comparison

The film grossed US$60 million over the weekend, making it the biggest launch for the franchise in 24 years. The previous record, set in 2010, was US$26 million for Resident Evil: Afterlife. Globally, the international debut generated US$48.3 million, totaling US$108.3 million worldwide. The production had a budget of US$75 million.

Critical and Audience Reception

The film holds 96% on Rotten Tomatoes and received a "B+" CinemaScore. These positive ratings indicate that both critics and viewers appreciated the new approach, which blends horror with humor and maintains the game's atmosphere.

Impact on the Film Industry

Resident Evil's performance demonstrates that game adaptations can be successful when they respect the original experience. Director Zach Cregger was recognized for bringing something "familiar and original" to audiences, reinforcing the importance of considering younger audiences, especially Generation Z, who drive box office sales.

Future Prospects for the Franchise

With the successful debut, Sony may plan new productions within the series, capitalizing on the renewed public interest. The film also paves the way for other game adaptations that seek a more faithful and engaging approach.

With information from Variety, Slate Magazine, The Guardian.
